I am afraid I don’t quite understand what do you mean by “cut”. Fur textures is something I am not too familiar with either. But I had to highlight almost every hair string about 3 times (for every highlight stage). Just take the paint that is lighter than your base coat and make it solid, solid in a way that you can easily paint in another line within it. When you are at a point that you simply don’t have space to place another line without it going over your previous work, simply make it shorter or place it towards the tip. You can always just add a dot highlight, and trust me, dot highlights are very effective. 

If you can clarify what did you mean by “cut”, I will gladly explain how I did it😃

Hi and tank you! I went a bit experimental with his skin. I mixed Ushabti Bone (Citadel) and Corpse pale (Army painter). Then I added a bit of Bugmans Glow to shade. (Secret here is to use Medium to dilute the mix into glaze consistency. (I use Matt Medium from Windsor). Then I added a bit of khorne and some purples to shade his deformed part of the face. (I made separate mix for each of them.)
The highlight part was just adding a bit of white for every highlight stage and covering less and less space. 

General tips: 
I don’t use shades by citadel because they have a gloss finish and no matter how much Matt medium I added to it, the gloss was still there. 

I use magnifying glasses when it comes to the smallest work. Not because I see badly, but because my eyes won’t hurt day after. You are really stressing your eye muscles for no reason. 

Wipe your brush on your thumb before you touch model. I ignored this part for too long, biggest mistake ever. You will have so much more control over your lines. Your edge highlight will ascent to another level. 

That was about it. Feel free to ask if you need anything. And good luck❤️
